title: “FATHER, FORGIVE THEM.”
paragraphs: “FATHER, FORGIVE THEM.”

The nails were still tearing His flesh…
And mercy was already flowing.

Not after the pain.
Not when the soldiers apologized.
Not when the crowd changed their minds.
Right there.

In the middle of the blood.
In the middle of the mockery.
In the middle of the cross.
“Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do.” — Luke 23:34
This is the scandal of grace.

The men who hammered the spikes into His wrists…
The soldiers gambling for His clothes…
The leaders sneering, “He saved others; let Him save Himself.”
Jesus did not answer with fire.
He answered with forgiveness.
Pause and feel the weight of that moment.

Every breath on the cross was torture.
Every word cost Him oxygen.
Every sentence was agony.
And the first recorded sentence from His bleeding lips was not judgment.
It was mercy.
Not “Father, destroy them.”
But:
“Father, forgive them.”
Why?
Because the cross was not just an execution.
It was a rescue mission.

The same people shouting for His death…
were the very people He came to save.
And here is the terrifying truth.
It was not only their sin that nailed Him there.
It was ours.

Our pride.
Our hidden lust.
Our lies.
Our anger.
Our quiet rebellion against God.
The cross exposes us.
But it also saves us.
Because while humanity was doing its worst…
Jesus was doing His best.

He was absorbing the punishment sin deserved.
He was standing in the place of the guilty.
He was opening the door of mercy.

Some scholars interpret that Jesus’ prayer may have been specifically for those who did not fully understand the magnitude of what they were doing. But Luke’s Gospel shows something even greater: forgiveness flowing outward, reaching anyone who will turn to Him.
Just look at what happens next in Luke 23.
A criminal hanging beside Him says:
“Jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom.”
And Jesus answers:
“Today you will be with me in paradise.” (Luke 23:43)
Do you see it?
The cross becomes the place where a dying criminal becomes a forgiven man.
Because Jesus was not only forgiving His killers.
He was purchasing forgiveness for the world.
For you.
For me.
For anyone willing to turn and trust Him.

No sin too dirty.
No past too heavy.
No shame too deep.
The cross says:
Mercy is still possible.
Right now.

If your heart is heavy today…
If guilt whispers that you are too far gone…
Listen again to the voice from the cross.
“Father, forgive them.”
That prayer is still echoing through history.
And the invitation still stands.

Turn to Christ.
Confess your sin.
Trust the One who bled for you.
Because the cross proves one unstoppable truth:
God’s mercy is louder than our worst mistakes.
And Jesus is still saving sinners.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
